# Purpose

This document explains a basic monthly sales analysis using R and a synthetic dataset. It demonstrates data organization, descriptive statistics, and visualization.

# Inputs

The dataset contains fictional monthly sales figures for January through June.

- `month`: Name of the month.
- `sales`: Monthly sales amount in Canadian dollars.

# Data Preparation

```{r data-preparation}
sales_data <- data.frame(
  month = c("January", "February", "March", "April", "May", "June"),
  sales = c(12000, 14500, 13200, 16800, 18500, 20100)
)

print(sales_data)
```

# Summary Statistics

```{r summary-statistics}
total_sales <- sum(sales_data$sales)
average_sales <- mean(sales_data$sales)

print(total_sales)
print(average_sales)
summary(sales_data)
```

# Visualization

```{r visualization}
barplot(
  sales_data$sales,
  names.arg = sales_data$month,
  main = "Monthly Sales Analysis",
  xlab = "Month",
  ylab = "Sales (CAD)",
  col = "skyblue",
  las = 2
)
```

# Outputs

The analysis produces a monthly sales table, total and average sales, descriptive statistics, and a bar chart comparing sales across six months.

# Conclusion

This project demonstrates how R can be used to organize, summarize, and visualize monthly sales data. The dataset is synthetic and is used only for educational purposes.
